headline: EMPEROR DRILLS 24.8M @ 7.0 G/T AU FROM 85M DEPTH — Duquesne West Junior Advances Open-Pit Resource Toward Multi-Million-Oz Target
snippet: Emperor Metals (CSE: AUOZ) reported DQ26-61 returning 24.8 metres at 7.0 g/t gold from approximately 85 metres vertical depth at the Duquesne West gold project in Quebec, the highest-grade intercept yet from the 66-hole 2026 program. With 55 of 66 holes now assayed across the near-surface open-pit target, Emperor is building toward a resource update on a property that hosts an existing 1.46-million-ounce inferred resource at 1.69 g/t — with the 2026 program designed to expand it substantially.

headline: LODESTAR'S MAIDEN NEVADA DRILL HITS GOLD AT ALL 4 TARGETS — 71.6m @ 0.9 g/t AuEq at Crown North Confirms District-Scale Potential at Gold Run
snippet: Lodestar Metals (TSXV: LSTR) confirmed gold-silver mineralisation at all four target areas — Robbers Knob, Gomes, Black Diamond and Crown North — in its 18-hole maiden drill program at the Gold Run project in Nevada, with the best intercept being 71.6 metres at 0.9 g/t gold-equivalent at Crown North. Finding economic mineralisation at every target tested in a maiden program is a rare result, suggesting Gold Run has the continuous mineralised system heap-leach-friendly Nevada projects typically require for scalable economics.

headline: GOLD MINERS POST BEST DAY IN 3 MONTHS — GDX SURGES 6.2% as Midterm Sweep Collapses Dollar, Extends Gold Above $4,000
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) surged 6.2% on November 4 — its largest single-day gain in nearly three months — as the Democratic congressional sweep sent the dollar to a one-month low and crushed Treasury yields, with spot gold holding at $4,047 after a 3% gain. The move implies the market is pricing in fiscal restraint and rate-cut odds that have historically preceded sustained mining sector re-ratings: when gold holds above $4,000 and miners add leverage, analysts typically call it the beginning rather than the end of a bull leg.

headline: RADISSON RELEASES 9 MORE O'BRIEN HOLES — 83% Hit Rate Across 137 Holes Into Former World-Class Abitibi High-Grade Mine
snippet: Radisson Mining (TSXV: RDS) announced nine additional drill holes extending high-grade gold mineralisation beneath and adjacent to the former O'Brien gold mine in Quebec's Abitibi camp, with an 83% hit rate across the 137 completed holes in its ongoing 140,000-metre step-out program. The company has successfully pushed the O'Brien gold system to 1.9 kilometres vertical depth — deeper than any drill program in the former mine's history — and the latest batch continues to confirm grade continuity of the classic Abitibi-style vein structures at those depths.

headline: HECLA CRUSHES Q3 ESTIMATES — $395M Revenue Beats $343M Forecast by 15%; EPS $0.22 vs $0.15; Shares JUMP 12%
snippet: Hecla Mining (NYSE: HL), North America's largest primary silver producer, beat both top-line and bottom-line Q3 2026 consensus estimates — revenue of $395 million versus the $343 million forecast, and adjusted EPS of $0.22 against the $0.15 expected — sending shares 12% higher. The result suggests Hecla's combination of silver leverage at $51/oz and ongoing cost discipline is translating directly into earnings outperformance, cementing its position as one of the highest-quality pure-silver equities in a metal approaching multi-decade highs.

headline: COPPER FALLS TO 2.5-MONTH LOW AS CHILE SLASHES 2026 OUTPUT FORECAST 8.4% — Cochilco Cuts to 5.3Mtpa; LME Hit $13,883 Before Midterm Bounce
snippet: LME three-month copper fell 2.4% to $14,000 per tonne on November 3 — touching $13,883, its weakest level since August 19 — as Chile's Cochilco simultaneously cut its 2026 national copper production forecast 8.4% to 5.3 million tonnes, compounding risk-off pressure from AI spending jitters. The metal bounced Wednesday on dollar weakness following the Democratic midterm sweep, but analysts argue the structural supply story — Cochilco's downgrade, Grasberg's delayed ramp-up, and planned Chilean investment of $105 billion through 2034 still years from output — sets a floor under a $14,000–$14,250 range.

headline: GOLD ANALYST: $4,000 IS A REBOUND TARGET, NOT A CEILING — Bearish Case Puts $3,500 Support in Sight Before Correction Completes
snippet: Even as gold recovers to $4,047 on midterm-driven dollar weakness, FXStreet notes that at least one analyst treats the $4,000 level as a rebound within a larger correction from January's $5,597 peak, targeting a slide toward $3,500 and potentially the low $3,000s before a final bottom. The technical picture shows gold back above $4,000 but still below its 20-day moving average, with $3,870 as key support; Friday's US jobs report is flagged as the next macro event that could break the near-term direction either way.

headline: MP MATERIALS REPORTS Q3 THURSDAY — REE Sector Eyes China Export Control Expiry as Consensus Sees -$0.01 EPS on $119M Revenue
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) reports Q3 2026 results after the bell on Thursday, November 5, with consensus sitting at a near-breakeven EPS of -$0.01 and $119 million in revenue — a report that lands less than a week before China's October 2025 rare-earth export control suspension expires on November 10. MP has beaten revenue estimates in each of the past two quarters; whether it can extend that run while the sector has sold off 6–10% in recent weeks will set the tone for rare-earth equities heading into the most consequential supply-chain decision of 2026.

headline: URANIUM ONE BREAKS INTO PARAGUAY — Maiden Exploration Begins at Yuty Prometeo-San Jose, Opening a New South American Uranium Frontier
snippet: Uranium One has begun its first-ever exploration program at the Yuty Prometeo-San Jose project in Paraguay following receipt of a prospection permit, marking the first organised uranium exploration in the country in decades. The project sits in a sedimentary basin analogous to uranium-bearing formations in neighbouring Argentina and Brazil — and Uranium One's entry into a new South American jurisdiction signals that the global feedstock search is expanding beyond the established Kazakh and Canadian belts as 70-plus reactors under construction worldwide tighten the long-term supply picture.

headline: ATHABASCA CAN'T SUPPLY THE NEXT NUCLEAR BUILD — Generation Uranium CEO: New Districts Need 15-Year Development Runway Starting Today
snippet: Generation Uranium's CEO argued in an InvestingNews interview that the global nuclear build-out — now at a 40-year high — requires uranium supply development well beyond the Athabasca Basin, since new production centers take 15 to 20 years from initial exploration to output. With spot uranium near $89/lb and long-term contracts increasingly rare, the CEO's argument that capital must move now into early-stage exploration outside traditional districts is gaining traction among investors who understand the lag between drilling and commercial production.

headline: AZIMUT LAUNCHES UPDATED PATWON GOLD RESOURCE IN JAMES BAY — 2023 NI 43-101 Used $1,800/oz Gold; 2026 Drilling Warrants Full Rework
snippet: Azimut Exploration (TSXV: AZM) announced it has commissioned a new NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate for its Patwon gold deposit in Québec's James Bay region following its 2026 diamond drilling campaign. The existing 2023 estimate was based on a gold price of US$1,800 per ounce — roughly 55% below current market levels — making an updated estimate essential for accurately reflecting the economic potential and potentially unlocking a preliminary economic assessment at a gold price environment that changes the project economics dramatically.

headline: IVANHOE MINES MISSES Q3 ON BOTH LINES — $263M Revenue Falls Short of $296M Expected; Kamoa-Kakula Copper Under Analyst Scrutiny
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines (TSX: IVN) reported Q3 2026 results that missed analyst expectations on both revenue ($263.84 million versus $295.97 million forecast) and EPS ($0.04 versus $0.0647 consensus), sending the stock lower. As the operator of Kamoa-Kakula — one of the world's highest-grade copper mines in the DRC — an Ivanhoe miss raises questions about production ramp-up pacing at the Phase 3 expansion and the capital intensity of maintaining top-tier output growth in a complex African jurisdiction.
